title: Blink (External LED)
description: Wire an LED and a 220 ohm resistor to your Arduino Uno on a breadboard, then run the classic Blink sketch to make it flash on and off once a second.

steps.clip: Let's gather what you need: an LED, a 220 ohm resistor, and a couple of jumper wires.
Push the resistor into the breadboard so its two legs land in two different columns.
hints: It doesn't matter which way round you place it — either leg can go in either hole.
Leave a free column or two next to it for the LED.

steps.clip: Push the LED into the breadboard next to the resistor, lining its long leg up with the resistor's free leg.
hints: The longer leg is the anode — put it in the same column as the resistor's free leg.
The LED only works one way round, so keep track of which leg is which.

steps.clip: The resistor's leg and the LED's long leg are already connected — they share a column on the breadboard.
hints: No wire needed here, just check they're in the same column.
This is the connection between the resistor and the LED's anode.

steps.clip: Run a wire from the resistor's other leg to digital pin 13 on the Arduino.
hints: Plug one end into the same column as the resistor's first leg.
Plug the other end into pin 13.

steps.clip: Run a wire from the LED's short leg to a GND pin on the Arduino.
hints: Plug one end into the same column as the LED's short leg, the cathode.
Plug the other end into any GND pin on the board.

steps.clip: Upload the code — your LED should blink on and off once a second.
